gen-luckiest-guy-gf-saira-semi-condensed: Saira Semi Condensed looks magnified even at modest sizes, with a weight that never wavers from word to word. And Luckiest Guy, loud and cheerful with poured-looking ink, gives that steadiness something to push against.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-secular-one:
Secular One has a heavy midsection that swallows most of the line's height.

Paging through paragraphs of it feels dense and solid, since every stroke keeps the same weight, while Luckiest Guy shouts cheerfully above in its poured, rounded ink.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-smooch-sans: Tight, tall and lean, Smooch Sans packs its line so closely that the gaps nearly vanish. But Luckiest Guy has diagonals as heavy as its verticals, so a long run of the plain sans feels light and quick underneath it.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-sofia-sans-condensed: Sofia Sans Condensed reads friendly and open, with a big x-height and curves that stop before closing their loops. Yet Luckiest Guy is the one built to shout, while the body font is built to keep a steady, quiet pace.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-tiny5: Luckiest Guy hits with a mean, high line and ink that looks poured at one width. But it is made for shouting, while Tiny5 is the one that carries the quieter text, its tall body making the ascenders look short.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-truculenta:
Luckiest Guy sets its mean line high and pours its ink thick.

Truculenta brings the opposite: a compact, crowded line with a tall x-height and rounded forms that stay open to the side, which makes the loud-and-snug pairing the strongest thing here.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-ubuntu: Ubuntu holds a lofty lowercase band, modern and businesslike in tone. Ubuntu stays low-key under Luckiest Guy, whose plain, unshaded lines and cheerful bluster do the shouting for both.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-viga: Loud, cheerful and poured thick, Luckiest Guy grabs the eye first. Viga follows with strokes free of hairlines and shadows, and capitals that barely rise above its lowercase, so the two never compete.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-voces: Cheerful is the first word for Luckiest Guy, whose rounded-nib look has no swelling at the stroke ends. But Voces does the quieter work, with tall lowercase and stems and hairlines in a close ratio that keep a plain sans line gentle.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-winky-rough:
Winky Rough sets its body height almost level with the capitals.

That sameness is the strongest thing here, since Luckiest Guy shouts with a high mean line and poured ink, and the body simply holds its ground below.
